additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与申诉程序
additionalTopics.statusLabel: 按不端行为日期区分申诉规则
additionalTopics.summary: All GenAI use must adhere to Academic Misconduct regulations in the Vancouver and Okanagan Academic Calendars; AI content detectors are strongly discouraged and Turnitin AI detection is disabled. Under Academic Calendar §11 (Appeals), the applicable Senate appeal rules depend on the date on which the alleged act of misconduct took place: for allegations of misconduct occurring on or after August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2, §11.4–§11.5), a student must submit a written appeal to the Registrar within 45 calendar days from the date the student receives the President's letter, giving a full explanation of the grounds and containing all documents the student intends to rely upon (with Registrar extension discretion if appropriate), heard by at least 5 committee members at Vancouver and at least 4 at Okanagan (unless the student consents to fewer), with written and oral submissions, legal counsel representation, and a support person; for allegations occurring prior to August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.3), the Registrar must receive written notification within 45 calendar days of the date of the President's letter and the student may be represented or assisted by any person, including legal counsel. For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. The reviewed Okanagan page has separate before/after headings but does not independently establish mixed-date case handling.
additionalTopics.scope: Academic misconduct regulations, AI detector restrictions, student advocacy services, and Vancouver/Okanagan Senate disciplinary appeals (post-August 1, 2019 vs pre-August 1, 2019 alleged misconduct regimes)
actions: Adhere strictly to UBC Vancouver and Okanagan Academic Calendar regulations regarding unauthorized assistance.

For disciplinary appeals involving alleged misconduct on or after August 1, 2019 (§11.2), submit a written appeal with full grounds and all relied-upon documents to the Registrar within 45 calendar days from the date you receive the President's letter.

additionalTopics.statusLabel: 参议院课程大纲法定要求
additionalTopics.summary: Faculty and staff may use GenAI in teaching and learning within legal, university, Faculty, and program-level boundaries. Effective September 1, 2026, Senate Policies V-130 (Vancouver) and O-130.1 (Okanagan) require syllabi for all credit-bearing courses (graduate-level theses and dissertation courses exempt) to include Academic Integrity and GenAI usage statements, provided within the first week of class unless created in consultation with the student(s) at the beginning of a course section (finalized prior to the drop-without-'W' deadline). Instructors must not upload student work or third-party copyright material to unapproved AI tools.
additionalTopics.scope: Instructional practice, credit-course syllabus requirements (Senate V-130 / O-130.1, subject to Section 4 consultation exception and graduate thesis exemption), and student IP protection
